output.brief: The rise in Corvane's mishandled bags is not mainly a handler problem. Since 1 September, bag tags printed on the new Fennick stock fail automatic reading about 12% of the time, against about 1.5% before. Transfer tags and Pelion tags are unaffected. Pelion uses the same Tessaly crew pool and its rate did not rise. On 14–16 October, counters that temporarily used the old Brackwater stock read fine, while kiosks on Fennick stock kept failing. The failed tags go to the manual encode desk, where waits grew from 7 to about 30 minutes. Of the encode-path bags that missed their flights, 91% reached the lateral after it closed. Tessaly's inexperienced crews may add some risk, but the data doesn't show them causing the rise. I'm fairly sure of this. I can't yet say whether the fault is the stock itself or how the printers are set for it. I'd also treat the printer-jam link as unproven. Don't issue the breach notice or withhold the fee. Return counters and kiosks to the Brackwater stock held in stores (about five weeks' supply). Get Teyra's printer-setting guidance and test Fennick stock separately before any defect claim. Ask HBAA about temporary extra encode capacity in the evening bank.
